headline: Reflect Orbital's space mirrors could jeopardize the night sky, shining as bright as 10,000 full moons
summary: Reflect Orbital plans to deploy giant space mirrors that will scatter light over tens of kilometers. This initiative raises concerns about light pollution and its potential impact on astronomical observations and natural ecosystems.
details: Reflect Orbital's space mirrors are designed to shine with immense brightness, equivalent to 10,000 full moons. These giant beams are intended to scatter light over areas spanning tens of kilometers.

The deployment of such powerful orbital reflectors raises significant concerns among scientists and environmentalists. Critics fear the mirrors could severely impact astronomical observations by increasing light pollution.

Beyond scientific implications, there are worries about the potential disruption to natural ecosystems. The altered night sky could affect nocturnal wildlife and human perception of the natural environment.

The long-term effects of large-scale space-based light sources remain a subject of ongoing debate and research. Experts are calling for careful consideration of the environmental and scientific consequences before deployment.

headline: Sandisk's new $2,200 NAS SSD lets you fill the drive every day for five years — 7.68TB M.2 flaunts eye-popping 14,000 TBW rati
summary: The Sandisk NAS 800 7.68TB M.2 NVMe SSD boasts an unprecedented 14 PBW endurance, allowing users to write 7.67TB daily for five years. Priced at $2,199.99, it sets a new standard for NAS storage.
details: Sandisk has launched its new NAS 600 SATA and NAS 800 NVMe SSD series, specifically targeting Network Attached Storage (NAS) devices. The top-tier Sandisk NAS 800 7.68TB model features an endurance rating of 14 PBW (Petabytes Written) and will retail for $2,199.99.

NAS users often rely on hard drives for capacity and affordability, but SSDs offer superior transfer throughput. While SSDs can act as performance accelerators, continuous 24/7 operation in NAS environments demands drives with exceptionally high endurance.

The Sandisk NAS 800 delivers some of the highest endurance ratings ever seen in a NAS SSD. Rated for 14 PBW over its lifespan, the 7.68TB drive allows users to write up to 7.67TB of data daily for five years under warranty. This translates to an impressive 1 Drive Write Per Day (DWPD).

To put this in perspective, consumer SSDs typically offer around 2,500 TBW, and even other NAS SSDs sometimes reach 5,000 TBW. The NAS 800's endurance places it in the same league as enterprise SSDs, which often exceed 10,000 TBW.

Beyond endurance, the NAS 600 and NAS 800 series deliver expected performance for their interfaces. The SATA III-based NAS 600 offers sequential speeds up to 560 MB/s read and 520 MB/s write. The PCIe 4.0 NAS 800 achieves up to 14,900 MB/s read and 13,200 MB/s write, with firmware optimized for NAS workloads.

Pricing for the NAS 600 starts at $179.99 for 500GB, scaling to $999.99 for the 4TB SKU. The NAS 800 960GB will cost $309.99, with the 7.68TB model at $2,199.99. Both series include a five-year warranty and are set to be available for purchase in September.
